candidateAssessment.label: Ancient cultures, literature and philosophical interpretation
candidateAssessment.reason: UCR offers substantial study of ancient material culture and democracy, classical myth and rhetoric, and ancient elements within literature, history and philosophy. The strongest composition combines these with interpretive and philosophical methods. Its advanced work nevertheless centres on broader philosophy, literary interpretation and art history, rather than sustained investigation of Greek and Roman texts, their transmission and their historical reception. The political alternative adds modern law and politics without establishing the claimed continuity from antiquity. These are valuable related studies, but neither forms a sufficiently close complete response to the integrated classical source research at the centre of this degree.

candidateAssessment.label: Antiquity, democracy and the politics of the present
candidateAssessment.reason: Ancient democratic heritage and political philosophy are real contributions. Comparative politics, international law, constitutional law, private law, EU law and peace/conflict supply modern institutions, cases and methods; their evidence does not support treating entire courses as classical reception or genealogies from Rome. Removing those overclaims reopens the organising concept, rather than merely its label.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden Classics studies Greek and Latin texts alongside the literature, history, philosophy and material culture of the ancient world. Students investigate how classical works were transmitted and interpreted and how antiquity influenced later societies.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial study of ancient material culture and democracy, classical myth and rhetoric, and ancient elements within literature, history and philosophy. These can support a broader humanities programme with interpretive and philosophical methods. Its advanced work would centre on broader philosophy, literary interpretation and art history, however, rather than sustained investigation of Greek and Roman texts, their transmission and their historical reception. Modern law and politics would add other subjects without supplying that classical research focus. We therefore show Leiden’s curriculum without presenting a UCR composition as a sufficiently close complete alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC illustrates the Ancient Philosophy specialisation. The language pathway assumes prior school-examination Latin and beginner Greek; placement determines each student’s language courses. Years one and two each contain 60 EC. The third year combines philosophy and religion in late antiquity, the Latin reading list, a Greek seminar, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC of approved open choice. The Stoa and late-antiquity courses require earlier philosophy study; the latter also requires first-year ancient history. The third-year seminar requires the first-year examination and a passed second-year Greek or Latin seminar; the reading list requires the first-year examination. The philosophy thesis must integrate Greek and/or Latin primary texts. Academic-skills mentoring and the thesis seminar are compulsory without additional credits. University approval and overlap rules apply to open choice.
